q: What emissions should an opencast coal mine report besides diesel?
title: Opencast coal mine: diesel and methane
short: Diesel for dumpers, shovels and drills is usually the largest on site source. Methane released from the coal seam is the second: the IPCC Tier 1 average for surface mining is 1.2 cubic metres per tonne mined, about 24 kg CO2e. Add explosives, grid power for conveyors, and any coal fires.
audience: Opencast coal mines and contractors in Korba, Talcher and Singrauli, and power plants reporting upstream coal emissions

ul: Diesel: litres from fuel logs x 2.68 kg CO2 per litre.
Seam methane: tonnes mined x emission factor, measured where possible.
Explosives, mainly ammonium nitrate based, from consumption records.
Electricity for conveyors and pumps x 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25.

p: IPCC 2006 gives low, average and high factors of 0.3, 1.2 and 2.0 cubic metres per tonne for surface mines, plus a small post mining amount. Convert at 0.67 kg per cubic metre and weight by the methane GWP.
If a contractor runs the fleet, its diesel is the contractor's Scope 1 and the mine's Scope 3, unless the mine supplies and controls the fuel.

example.title: Worked example: methane per tonne
lines: 1.2 m3 CH4 per tonne x 0.67 kg per m3 = 0.80 kg CH4
0.80 kg x 29.8 (AR6 fossil methane GWP100) = about 24 kg CO2e per tonne mined
example.note: Uses the IPCC average; a measured factor for your seam is better.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel, electricity and freight invoices into a dated, fingerprinted record per site, so each figure you send a buyer can be traced back to the documents behind it.
